projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The gradual decline and stabilization of the connected device count to 23, combined with zero camera motion, aligns with a normal Thursday evening routine where the household is settled indoors and devices are naturally entering sleep mode.

A sustained presence count of 24-25 devices over four hours with zero camera activity strongly suggests either a gathering in a camera-blind area, disabled cameras, or an IoT network anomaly rather than normal household movement. Steve should verify camera functionality and check if unexpected guests or network devices are inflating the count.

The sustained count of 17–20 connected devices paired with zero camera motion for four hours during typical active hours suggests either a camera malfunction, a large gathering in an unmonitored area, or a false presence count. Steve should verify camera functionality and check if guests are present.

The sustained presence count of 17–20 devices paired with zero camera motion for four hours suggests either a stationary gathering (e.g., guests or a movie night) or a Wi-Fi tracking anomaly. This warrants verification to rule out sensor issues or unlogged visitors.

The persistent high device count (18-20) paired with zero camera activity for four hours suggests either a camera system malfunction or that the entire household has congregated in a camera-blind zone, warranting a quick system check to ensure security coverage isn't compromised.

The gradual decline to a stable count of 17 connected devices, combined with zero camera activity over the past four hours, strongly indicates the home is currently unoccupied, aligning with Thursday school and work schedules. If the family expected to be home, this warrants a quick check on camera functionality or confirming everyone's whereabouts.

The drop to ~20 devices by 08:30 followed by a stable count aligns with the children’s Thursday school departure, while the persistent ~20 devices and zero camera motion suggest the adults remain home and the kids left via a camera-blind route or their devices entered airplane mode. This appears to be a normal routine, but worth confirming to ensure the departure was logged and cameras are operating correctly.

The drop in connected devices to ~20 at 08:30, paired with zero camera activity throughout the morning, indicates the family has likely already left for school and work. This confirms the home is currently unoccupied and aligns with expected Thursday morning routines.

The sharp drop in connected mobile devices from 25 to 19 between 08:23 and 08:33, combined with the Thursday morning timeframe, strongly indicates the family has quietly left for school and work. The remaining ~19 devices are likely stationary smart home/IoT equipment, confirming the household is now empty.

The network consistently reports 25–28 connected devices, which is unusually high for a four-person household and may indicate extensive IoT sprawl or untracked guests. A brief spike to 28 around 06:59 followed by a drop to 25 suggests a temporary connection that has since resolved.
